newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 97/98 car exports seen flat to lower -- JAMA.
newsitem.headline: Japan 97/98 car exports seen flat to lower -- JAMA.

text.p: Japan's vehicle exports in the year starting on April 1 are seen remaining flat or slightly lower than in the current year, Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA) chairman Yoshifumi Tsujii told reporters on Wednesday.

Asked whether Japan's automakers would be forced to boost exports in and after April in order to offset a likely decline in domestic car sales, Tsuji said: "Car exports in 1997/98 will remain flat or slightly below the year-ago level."
Japan's vehicle exports to the United States rose 75.3 percent to 124,834 in January, marking the fifth successive month they have gained on a year-on-year basis.
Japan's vehicle output is seen just above 10 million units in 1997/98, down from an estimated 10.65 million units seen for the current year, the JAMA chairman said.

The current high backlog of orders should help keep domestic vehicle sales to just over seven million units in 1997/98. But that is still lower than an estimated 7.27 million units in 1996/97, when sales grew 5.4 percent year-on-year, he said.
A planned sales tax rise in April is likely to have a full effect on domestic car sales in May or June, he said.

Tsuji said domestic sales in the January-March period are estimated to total 2.16 million units, up 9.8 percent from the same quarter a year earlier, surpassing the record sales of 2.02 million units for the quarter marked in 1991.
The car sales are seen growing, partly because customers are rushing to buy cars in the run-up to the planned sales tax rise to five percent from current three percent on April 1.
JAMA expects sales of imported cars to remain flat in 1997/98 from a year earlier given the current slowdown in sales.
